title: Systemic AcciMap: Synthetic pump fire, 2024
audience: Corporate HSE, site leadership and the investigation team
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document

bottom_line.text: The findings reach company management (level 3) and no higher: nothing is placed at the regulator or government levels.
The spares programme at level 3 (OR 2.2) links down to the missing guidance at level 4 and the omitted step at level 5.

items.text: Placements above the company level are inferred from codes and departments. A person confirms them before this map is shared.

nodes.label: L1 Government policy and budgeting (0 findings)
L2 Regulatory bodies and associations (0 findings)
L4 Technical and operational management (1 finding)
L5 Physical processes and actor activities (1 finding)

sections.heading: Levels the export does not reach

items.text: Level 1 (Government policy and budgeting) and level 2 (Regulatory bodies and associations) have no placements. An empty level is a question for the organisation, not a finding that nobody there contributed.

items.lesson: Seals were bought with no approved specification, and the gap carried down to the work at the pump.
items.explanation: OR 2.2 at level 3 links to SV 1.4 at level 4 (1 mention), which links to the omitted step at level 5 [EVD-0003].

items.question: Is level 3 (company management) right for the spares programme finding?
items.why: Level 3 is inferred from the HFACS level 4 code, not from what the export says about who decided.
items.good_evidence: The corporate purchasing standard and its approval record

items.question: Did the regulator's inspections play a part at level 2 (regulatory bodies and associations)?
items.why: Level 2 is a gap: no finding is tagged to a regulator.
